subject: Discovery recap: Observability & evals — dashboards, tracing, golden prompts
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Elena Vasilev <elena@finlytics.com>, Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: Observability & evals — dashboards, tracing, golden prompts

Hi Elena / Rajesh — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our 45-minute discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. I copied Ben (AE), Dev (SE) and Marissa (CS) so we can move the technical and commercial threads in parallel.

Summary of pain & current stack
- Pain: Regression spikes after model rollouts; poor visibility into sample-level failures and prompt drift.
- Current stack: In-house logging (ELK) + a homegrown “sanity” job for prompt checks; no fine-grained trace correlation to token-level inference.
- Usage: ~15M tokens/mo, batchy inference with occasional low-latency endpoints for interactive flows.

Success criteria you called out
1) Dashboarding: single-pane observability for per-route latency, per-model quality deltas, and sample-level failure drilldown.
2) Tracing hooks: ability to attach request->KV-cache->response traces to correlate latency and quality regressions.
3) Golden prompt sets: canonical test prompts for nightly/eval regression checks and alerting on drift.
4) Rollout guardrails: canary evaluation, automatic rollback on quality regression, and manual override option.

Recommended next steps (proposed timeline)
- 1) Tech deep-dive (30–45 min) with Dev to walk through tracing hooks + Docker/K8s environment details — proposed Wed 4/28. (Owner: Dev)
- 2) Shared M.A.P. (mutual action plan) with milestones & success criteria — I attached a draft (MAP-FinLytics-v1.xlsx). (Owner: Olga + FinLytics)
- 3) Dashboard mock (static PNG) showing suggested panels for early validation. (Attached: dashboard-mockup.png).
- 4) Pilot plan: 4-week eval with guardrails and golden prompt regression checks; we can scope credits if needed. (Owner: Ben / Marissa)

Open questions we need from you before the deep-dive
- Can you share a sample of 50 failing requests (anonymized) for golden prompt alignment?
- Which VPC/region will you prefer for a pilot (us-west-2 or eu-west-1)?
- Any specific compliance constraints (e.g., data residency, logging retention) we should bake into the pilot?

Attachments: dashboard-mockup.png (image/png), MAP-FinLytics-v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Thanks — looking forward to the technical session.

—
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Date: 2027-04-25T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Observability & evals — dashboards, tracing, golden prompts

Hi Olga — thanks for the clear summary, this captures the discussion perfectly. A couple quick clarifications:
- We can export 50 anonymized failing requests by EOD Monday.
- Pilot region: us-west-2 is preferred.
- Retention: logs must be retained for 90 days, with an option to archive to our S3 for 1 year.

Wed 4/28 10:00 PT works for a tech deep-dive — please send an invite.

Elena
Director of ML Ops, FinLytics
elena@finlytics.com
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Elena Vasilev <elena@finlytics.com>, Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@finlytics.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Observability & evals — dashboards, tracing, golden prompts

Elena / Rajesh — looking forward to the deep-dive tomorrow. A few notes so we can use the session efficiently:
- For tracing hooks we prefer a lightweight request header (x-rwi-trace-id) that you can propagate through your orchestration layer; I’ll share a short snippet to drop into your inference client.
- For golden prompt regression we recommend a JSONL format with: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_top_k (if applicable), rubric_tags. 50 samples is a perfect starting point.
- Dashboard: I’ll bring a prototype that maps token-latency histograms + sample quality deltas (per-prompt) so you can see regressions at a glance.

Shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-finlytics-observability — I’ve added a README and the tracing-snippet.md.

See you 4/28 10:00 PT.

—
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: FinLytics qualification + next commercial steps

Olga / Marissa — quick internal note after Elena confirmed timeline & retention requirement. Qualification summary:
- Account: FinLytics (mid-market, ML-heavy, clear pain in regression detection).
- TAM: ~15M tokens/mo, potential for Dedicated in 6–9 months if pilot succeeds.
- Must-haves: 90-day retention, us-west-2 pilot, ability to attach traces to token-level samples.

Commercial next steps:
1) Offer 4-week pilot credits (ask: $10k equivalent) — I’ll run this by pricing.
2) Send a simple SOW with pilot scope + success criteria pulled from Olga’s MAP.
3) Prepare a follow-up call for Exec Sponsor intro if pilot hits week-2 milestones.

Assigning owners: Pilot credits & SOW (Ben), Tech sessions & pilot onboarding (Dev), Success criteria tracking (Marissa).

I’ll coordinate pricing approval today and update the deal in HubSpot (DEAL-2027-041-FTLYTICS).
